messages:
support_jordan: Hey team, customer acme-inc reports sudden p99 jumps on the text-generation route since last deploy. p95 is stable ~120ms but p99 up from 450ms to ~1.6s. Happening on hosted-api in us-west1. They see spikes across several keys.

eng_sre_maya: Thanks — can you paste the example request and any trace ids? Also did they change traffic pattern?

support_jordan: Example curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate` Trace: trace=acme-4498-req-72. Customer says most requests are tiny (short prompts).

eng_runtime_lee: On it. Early hypothesis: aggregation window / batch_timeout got increased in the deploy (we bumped aggregation_window_ms 8->30 for throughput experiments). That can increase tail latency for tiny payloads if fast-path not triggered.

infra_oliver: I see corresponding serving logs: a lot of requests sitting in batcher queue for ~25-30ms before release, then single-item batches for many requests. Tail aligns with aggregation_window_ms.

obs_bot: Alert: route=/v1/generate p99 increased from 0.45s -> 1.62s at 2026-03-16T21:12Z. Related deploy: deploy-2026-03-16-agg-win-tune.

support_jordan: Customer also mentioned intermittent auth 401s right before spikes — could be token refresh retries contributing to burstiness. Not sure if related.

eng_sre_maya: Good to flag. Retries + batching wait can amplify tail. Need repro steps: can we simulate high QPS of tiny prompts with 0.75 token median?

eng_runtime_lee: Repro command I used locally: `hey -n 2000 -c 40 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -m POST -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://staging.redwood.test/v1/generate` with aggregation_window_ms=30 produced p99~1.5s. With aggregation_window_ms=8 p99~520ms.

eng_sre_maya: So we confirmed. Root cause: raising aggregation_window to increase throughput for larger prompts increased the waiting time for tiny requests; small-request fast-path didn't kick in for this model/route due to `min_batch_fill=2` and `small_request_fastpath=false` in config.

product_sam: Why was small_request_fastpath disabled? That was part of the throughput experiment to keep GPU utilization stable across multi-tenant workloads. We can roll it back per-route.

infra_oliver: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert aggregation_window_ms to previous value globally (affects throughput), 2) enable fast-path for /v1/generate, 3) set per-tenant override for acme-inc to lower aggregation window. Recommend 2+3 as minimal blast radius.

support_jordan: Customer asked for ETA — can we do a hotfix toggle?

eng_runtime_lee: I can flip `small_request_fastpath=true` for that model in prod and set `aggregation_window_ms=10` for that route. That should bring p99 under 600ms. I'll put config change behind a canary (10% traffic) then ramp.

eng_sre_maya: Also need to check token refresh/retry behavior. @customer_ops_anna can you verify whether acme moved to our new short-lived tokens yesterday? If token refresh storms are creating bursts of retries that fill the queue, that'd compound tail latency.

customer_ops_anna: Confirmed acme rotated to short tokens at 20:45Z. Their SDK refresh path had a bug causing simultaneous refresh attempts under some race conditions. They pushed a server-side fix; I'll coordinate to confirm no more refresh storms.

eng_runtime_lee: Plan: (1) Enable fast-path for route /v1/generate (canary 10% now). (2) Per-tenant aggregation_window_ms override -> acme-inc=10ms. (3) Monitor p95/p99 for next 30m. (4) If successful, rollout wider. I'll open a quick PR to infra-config and apply.

infra_oliver: Applying canary change now. Patch id cfg-5821.

obs_bot: Note: canary config applied to 10% of /v1/generate traffic at 2026-03-16T21:20Z.

eng_sre_maya: We'll need to communicate to support and customer. @support_jordan share expected improvement numbers with acme: p99 -> ~500-700ms after change.

support_jordan: Sent message to acme. They replied: "thanks, please keep us posted."

eng_runtime_lee: Canary metrics after 8 minutes: canary p99=540ms, control p99=1.58s. Throughput stable. No increase in token errors.

eng_sre_maya: Good. Roll to 50% then 100% over next 20m if no regressions. Also add a targeted test to our CI to run tiny-prompt load test with both fast-path enabled/disabled to prevent future regressions.

product_sam: I'll add a product note to the rollout docs: mention tradeoffs when increasing aggregation_window_ms and recommend enabling small_request_fastpath for low-latency routes.

infra_oliver: Rolled to 100% at 21:45Z. cfg-5821 deployed.

obs_bot: route=/v1/generate p99 back to 0.62s at 2026-03-16T21:47Z.

eng_sre_maya: Follow-ups: - eng_runtime_lee to add per-route default config in infra repo - customer_ops_anna to confirm acme token refresh fix - support_jordan to close ticket if customer confirms improvement. Owners added to the incident doc.

support_jordan: Acme confirmed improvement and we'll keep monitoring. Closing escalation pending 24h good signal. Thanks team :tada:
